title: Shared definitions
description: Vocabularies shared across the pipeline. The enums here exist so that defect identity is computed from constrained values rather than free text -- see DESIGN.md section 2 on fingerprint stability.

persona_id.description: Filename stem of a card in personas/, e.g. 'time-starved-parent'.

scenario_id.description: Filename stem of a scenario in scenarios/, e.g. 'checkout-interrupted'.

perturbation.description: Something that happens TO the session at a fixed step, decided before the run starts. Sealed into run.json with the rest of the scenario, injected by the persona-drift-check hook when the step is reached, and recorded in session.jsonl as a `perturbation` record. The gate checks that every perturbation that fell due was recorded, on time, exactly once.

at_step.description: Applied immediately after step N is recorded, so step N+1 is the first thing the persona does under it.

do.description: A closed set, so that runs with the same perturbation are comparable and so the hook can tell the agent what to actually do to the device.

for.description: How long it lasts: seconds ('45s'), minutes ('2m'), or steps ('3 steps'). Omit for instantaneous perturbations such as rotate or kill.

note.description: The in-world cause, in plain words ('the train goes into a tunnel'). Shown to user-agent with the perturbation; never copied into the session log.

digest.description: Content hash binding one artifact to another, so a downstream step cannot be run against a different input than the one it claims.

surface.description: Normalized screen or route identifier, e.g. 'settings/notifications'. Deliberately coarse: it is a fingerprint input, and free-form surface names are the main cause of fingerprint churn.

action_class.description: What kind of interaction this was. A closed set, because it is a fingerprint input.

symptom_class.$comment: 'access_barrier' covers accessibility failures. It is in the taxonomy on purpose: DESIGN.md section 1 names accessibility as the example of a blind spot shared by proposer and reviewer, and a named slot in a required enum is a weak but real prompt to consider the category. It does not solve the problem -- an agent can still never select it.
symptom_class.description: Coarse symptom taxonomy. A fingerprint input, so the set is closed and stable across versions.

fingerprint.description: Stable defect identity: sha256 over (surface, action_class, symptom_class), truncated, with a version prefix. Recomputed and verified by the review gate -- an agent cannot mint a fingerprint that dodges cross-run matching.

evidence_ref.description: A pointer to something that actually exists. Findings without at least one of these fail validation -- the cheapest available guard against fabricated defects.

steps.description: One step number, or an inclusive [start, end] range. Resolved against the session log by the review gate.

path.description: Path relative to the run directory. The review gate checks that the file exists.

severity.description: How much this hurts the persona if it is real. Impact only. Deliberately shares no words with `confidence`, so that 'I am unsure' cannot be spelled using this scale.

confidence.description: How likely it is that this is real at all. Epistemic only. Deliberately shares no words with `severity`. DESIGN.md section 2: conflating the two silently downgrades genuine high-severity findings.
